clinician.trajectory_summary: A 21-year-old woman presented with subjective visual impairment and blurry vision for 3 weeks with no abnormalities found on prior ophthalmologic examinations. Six weeks after initial symptoms, she developed lower limb weakness and clinical signs of transverse myelitis. Spinal cord MRI revealed lesions extending over 3 vertebral segments. NMO-IgG antibody serology was positive, confirming the diagnosis of Devic’s syndrome (neuromyelitis optica).
